description: The macro-release numeric-surprise mechanism's TAUGHT DATA + the surprise-decode RULE (MACRO_SURPRISE_PREREG.md). A macro print (CPI/NFP) is a NUMBER whose forecast relevance is its SURPRISE vs expectation. The mechanical reads (macro_surprise.py) turn a print into a MacroSurpriseReading{series, surprise_sign, market} (surprise_sign = +1 if released ABOVE prior/trend, -1 below, 0 equal) -- this is I/O arithmetic, no decision. WHICH STANCE a (series, surprise_sign) is, is TAUGHT DATA: one MacroSurpriseSign node per (series, surprise_sign) carrying (stance, band_sign, direction, attr), authored at teach time (macro_codebook_entries: band_sign = surprise_sign * hawkish_sign, stance/direction table lookups) -- exactly the ToM arm's (symbol, motion) -> (stance, sign) CBSpeechAct codebook pattern. The DECISION -- which stance a surprise is -- is the seed RULE `ib_decode_macro_surprise`, an Eq-join of a MacroSurpriseReading's (series, surprise_sign) against a MacroSurpriseSign codebook entry, minting the SAME StanceReading shape the ToM arm's ib_decode_stance rule mints (stance/sign/direction/attr pulled OFF the joined codebook node, so macro-surprise COMPOSES with the ToM decode on the SAME <stance>_stance_for:<market> CAN Concept. No new belief mechanism; strict reuse of the stance Concepts + concept_apply_evidence; no Python computes the stance/direction.

rules.name: ib_decode_macro_surprise
rules.comment: THE DECISION: a MacroSurpriseReading{series, surprise_sign, market} whose (series, surprise_sign) matches a MacroSurpriseSign codebook entry mints a StanceReading, pulling the stance/band_sign/direction/attr OFF the codebook entry (ms) -- NOT off the reading. The reading carries only the series + the bare surprise sign (I/O arithmetic: released above/below/inline the expectation); WHICH STANCE that (series, surprise_sign) is, is TAUGHT DATA on the MacroSurpriseSign node (band_sign = surprise_sign * hawkish_sign, stance/direction table lookups, authored at teach time by macro_codebook_entries -- the same mechanical expansion frame.codebook_entries does for the ToM codebook). This mirrors ib_decode_stance exactly: there the (symbol, motion) join pulls (stance, sign, direction) off the CBSpeechAct; here the (series, surprise_sign) join pulls them off the MacroSurpriseSign. Eq-join on series AND surprise_sign, guarded once per (macro_reading) by Not(Exists already-decoded). No surface-word cue matching; no Python computes the stance/direction -- the rule reads it off the joined codebook node.
